title: Mala's three objects
source: School paper question (Mala's objects K, L, M)
pageIntro: Test all three pairs on the bench, then answer.
stem:
Mala had three objects, K, L and M. She placed two different objects beside each other each time and recorded what happened.

Which of the following could objects K, L and M be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
K and L→ ← attract
L and M→ ← attract
K and M← → repel
hints: Which pair repels? What kind of objects can push each other away?
K and M are settled. L is pulled by both. Which options let L be pulled by a magnet?
key: Repel is the one result that proves both objects are magnets. Attract only tells you at least one of the pair is a magnet.

options.pick: L as a magnet explains why it attracts both K and M, and a magnet beside a steel block gives a strong reaction.
options.why: Steel is only pulled by magnets. It can never push anything away, so a steel K and a magnet M cannot repel.

options.pick: K is the magnet pulling steel L, and iron M is a magnetic material too, so it seems to belong with them.
options.why: Iron and steel are magnetic materials, not magnets. A magnet can only attract an iron block, so K and M would attract, not repel.

options.pick: Start with K and M. They repel, so both are magnets. L is pulled by both of them, which a steel block is.
options.why: Repel is only possible between two magnets, and a steel block is attracted to either magnet. L could also be a third magnet, but only this option fits all three results.

options.pick: L is a magnet that pulls both K and M. Steel and iron are different materials, so they might push each other.
options.why: Steel and iron are both magnetic materials. Two magnetic materials show no force on each other, so K and M would show nothing at all, not repel.

title: Wei Jie's three objects
pageIntro: Test all three pairs, then answer.
stem:
Wei Jie had three objects, P, Q and R. He placed two different objects beside each other each time and recorded what happened.

Which of the following could objects P, Q and R be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
P and Q→ ← attract
Q and Rno force
P and R→ ← attract
hints: One object attracts both of the others. Could it be the magnet?
Q and R show no force on each other. If one of them were a magnet, what would it do to the other?
key: A magnet pulls every iron or steel block, and two such blocks do not affect each other. The object that pulls everything is the magnet.

options.pick: Q is the magnet and pulls P. Iron and steel are both magnetic, so P and R should pull each other.
options.why: Iron and steel are magnetic materials, not magnets, so they show no force on each other. Also, a magnet Q would pull steel R, but Q and R showed no force.

options.pick: P is a magnet that pulls steel R. Plastic Q shows no force with R, which matches the Q and R result.
options.why: P and Q attracted, but a magnet shows no force with plastic. Matching one result is not enough; every result has to fit.

options.pick: R is the magnet and pulls steel P. Iron Q is magnetic too, so it seems to belong.
options.why: A magnet pulls every iron block, so R would attract Q, but you saw no force. Steel P and iron Q would also show no force, but you saw attract.

options.pick: Q and R show no force on each other, so neither is a magnet. P pulls both, so P is the magnet.
options.why: A magnet attracts iron and steel blocks, and two such blocks do not affect each other. All three results fit.

title: Aisha's three objects
pageIntro: Test all three pairs, then answer.
stem:
Aisha had three objects, X, Y and Z. She placed two different objects beside each other each time and recorded what happened.

Which of the following could objects X, Y and Z be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
X and Yno force
Y and Zno force
X and Z→ ← attract
hints: Which object shows no force with both of the others? What kind of material does a magnet have no effect on?
Only X and Z attract. Which of them is the magnet?
key: An object that shows no force with a magnet is non-magnetic. Find the magnet first; it pulls every iron or steel block.

options.pick: X and Z attract because iron and steel are both magnetic. Y is a magnet that just sits in the middle.
options.why: Iron and steel do not pull each other. A magnet Y would also pull both X and Z, but Y showed no force with either.

options.pick: Y shows no force with anything, so it is not magnetic. X and Z attract, so X is the magnet pulling iron Z.
options.why: A magnet has no effect on wood and pulls iron. All three results fit.

options.pick: X is the magnet because something attracts. Steel and plastic seem like ordinary blocks.
options.why: A magnet pulls steel, so X and Y would attract, but you saw no force. Plastic Z is not pulled, so X and Z would show no force, but you saw attract.

options.pick: Plastic Y shows no force with anything. Steel and iron are both magnetic, so X and Z attract.
options.why: Steel and iron are magnetic materials, not magnets. With no magnet in the set, nothing can attract.

title: Priya's three objects
pageIntro: Test all three pairs, then answer.
stem:
Priya had three objects, A, B and C. She placed two different objects beside each other each time and recorded what happened.

Which of the following could objects A, B and C be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
A and B← → repel
A and C← → repel
B and C→ ← attract
hints: Look at the two pairs that repel. Which object is in both?
Can a magnet attract one object and repel another? Think about which poles face each other.
key: Two magnets can attract or repel, depending on which poles face each other. Seeing attract does not mean one object is a plain block.

options.pick: A repels both B and C, so A, B and C are all magnets. B and C attract because unlike poles face each other.
options.why: Repel only happens between two magnets, and every object is in a repelling pair. Two magnets can attract as well as repel.

options.pick: B and C attract, so one of them could be a steel block pulled by a magnet.
options.why: Two magnets can attract too. And A and C repel, which a steel block can never do.

options.pick: B and C attract, so they are the magnets. A is the odd one out, so it could be steel.
options.why: A steel block can only be pulled, never pushed. A would attract both B and C, but it repelled them.

options.pick: A and C repel, so they are magnets. B and C attract, so B seems to be a steel block.
options.why: A and B repel, which steel cannot do. B must be a magnet too, and it attracts C because unlike poles face each other.

title: Daniel's three objects
pageIntro: Test all three pairs, then answer.
stem:
Daniel had three objects, D, E and F. He placed two different objects beside each other each time and recorded what happened.

Which of the following could objects D, E and F be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
D and E← → repel
E and Fno force
D and Fno force
hints: Start with the repelling pair. What are D and E?
Magnets pull iron and steel. What kind of object shows no force with a magnet?
key: No force with a magnet means non-magnetic. Two magnets never ignore each other.

options.pick: Plastic F shows no force, which fits. D is a magnet and E is steel, so they react differently.
options.why: D and E repel, but a magnet and a steel block can only attract.

options.pick: D and E repel, so both are magnets. Steel F does not repel, so no force seems to fit.
options.why: Not repelling is not the same as no force. A magnet pulls steel, so F would attract both D and E.

options.pick: D and E repel, so both are magnets. F shows no force with either, so it is not magnetic.
options.why: Magnets have no effect on plastic. All three results fit.

options.pick: D and E repel, so they are magnets. F could be a magnet too that happens to show no force beside them.
options.why: Two magnets placed beside each other always push or pull. F would attract or repel D and E, but you saw no force.

title: Three objects that all react
stem:
Three objects, A, B and C, were placed beside each other two at a time. The results are shown.

Which of the following could objects A, B and C be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
A and B→ ← attract
A and C← → repel
B and C← → repel
key: Every object here is in a repelling pair, so every object is a magnet. Two magnets attract when unlike poles face each other.

options.pick: A and B attract, so one of them could be a steel block pulled by a magnet.
options.why: B and C repel. A steel block can never push anything away, so B must be a magnet.

options.pick: A and B attract, so A could be an iron block pulled by magnet B.
options.why: A and C repel, and an iron block can never repel. A must be a magnet.

options.pick: A and C repel, and B and C repel, so A, B and C are all magnets. A and B attract because unlike poles face each other.
options.why: Only magnets repel, and every object is in a repelling pair. Two magnets can attract too.

options.pick: A and B look like the magnets, and C is the odd one out.
options.why: C repels both A and B. A magnet shows no force at all with plastic, so C cannot be plastic.

title: One object pulls both
stem:
Three objects, P, Q and R, were placed beside each other two at a time. The results are shown.

Which of the following could objects P, Q and R be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
P and Q→ ← attract
Q and R→ ← attract
P and Rno force
key: The object in both attracting pairs is the magnet. The two objects that show no force on each other are not magnets.

options.pick: R is the magnet, and iron and steel are both magnetic, so P and Q pull each other.
options.why: Iron and steel blocks show no force on each other. Also, magnet R would pull iron P, but P and R showed no force.

options.pick: P and R show no force, so neither is a magnet. Q attracts both, so Q is the magnet.
options.why: A magnet pulls iron and steel, and an iron block and a steel block show no force on each other. All three results fit.

options.pick: P is the magnet pulling Q, and Q and R are iron and steel, which seem to pull each other.
options.why: An iron block and a steel block do not pull each other. And magnet P would pull steel R, but P and R showed no force.

options.pick: Q is the magnet pulling steel P, and R is the leftover object.
options.why: Q and R attract, but a magnet shows no force with plastic.

title: The object that does nothing
stem:
Three objects, X, Y and Z, were placed beside each other two at a time. The results are shown.

Which of the following could objects X, Y and Z be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
X and Yno force
Y and Z← → repel
X and Zno force
key: Y and Z repel, so both are magnets. An object that shows no force with a magnet is non-magnetic.

options.pick: Y and Z repel so they are magnets, and X is something that is not a magnet.
options.why: A magnet pulls every steel block, so X would attract both Y and Z. You saw no force.

options.pick: Y and Z are magnets, and X could be a magnet that just did not react.
options.why: Two magnets beside each other always push or pull. X would attract or repel Y and Z.

options.pick: Iron is not a magnet, so it seems right for the object that does nothing.
options.why: Iron is a magnetic material. A magnet pulls every iron block, so X would attract Y and Z.

options.pick: Y and Z repel, so both are magnets. X shows no force with either magnet, so X is non-magnetic.
options.why: Magnets have no effect on wood. All three results fit.

title: Only one pair reacts
stem:
Three objects, J, K and L, were placed beside each other two at a time. The results are shown.

Which of the following could objects J, K and L be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
J and K→ ← attract
K and Lno force
J and Lno force
key: Check every option against all three results. L shows no force with either object, so L cannot be a magnet, iron or steel if J or K is a magnet.

options.pick: J and K attract, so they could be magnets with unlike poles facing, and L a third magnet.
options.why: Two magnets always push or pull. L showed no force with J or K, so L cannot be a magnet here.

options.pick: J and K attract, so one of them is a magnet. L shows no force with either, so L is non-magnetic.
options.why: Magnet J pulls steel K, and neither has any effect on wood. All three results fit.

options.pick: J is a magnet pulling steel K, and L is iron, another magnetic material.
options.why: A magnet pulls every iron block. J would attract L, but J and L showed no force.

options.pick: Steel and iron are both magnetic, so J and K pull each other.
options.why: Steel and iron blocks do not pull each other. With no magnet among J and K, nothing could attract.

title: A repelling pair and a third object
stem:
Three objects, A, B and C, were placed beside each other two at a time. The results are shown.

Which of the following could objects A, B and C be?
figure:
Pair placed beside each otherWhat happened
A and B← → repel
B and C→ ← attract
A and C→ ← attract
key: A and B repel, so both are magnets. C is pulled by both magnets, which an iron or steel block would be.

options.pick: A is the magnet, and B and C are magnetic materials that react to it.
options.why: A and B repel, and a steel block can never push anything away. B must be a magnet.

options.pick: B is the magnet, and iron and steel are both magnetic, so all three react.
options.why: A and B repel, which an iron block can never do. Also, iron A and steel C would show no force, but you saw attract.

options.pick: A and B repel, so both are magnets. C is pulled by both, which an iron block is.
options.why: Only magnets repel, and a magnet attracts every iron block. All three results fit.

options.pick: A and B repel, so both are magnets, and C is the third object.
options.why: C attracts both magnets, but a magnet shows no force at all with plastic.

title: Two objects repel
stem:
Two objects, P and Q, are placed beside each other. They push each other away.

Which statement must be true?
key: Repel is only possible between two magnets.

options.text: One is a magnet and the other is a steel block.
options.pick: Steel reacts strongly to magnets, so a magnet and steel seem likely.
options.why: A magnet can only pull a steel block, never push it away.

options.text: One is a magnet and the other is an iron block.
options.pick: Iron is a magnetic material, so it reacts to a magnet.
options.why: A magnet can only pull an iron block. Iron never repels.

options.text: One is a magnet and the other is a plastic block.
options.pick: If a magnet does not pull something, it might push it away instead.
options.why: A magnet shows no force at all with plastic: no pull and no push.

options.text: P and Q are both magnets.
options.pick: Ask which objects can push each other away. Only magnets can.
options.why: Like poles of two magnets repel. Nothing else can push another object away like this.

title: Two objects attract
stem:
Two objects, P and Q, are placed beside each other. They pull towards each other.

Which statement must be true?
key: Attract tells you at least one of the pair is a magnet. It does not tell you what the other object is.

options.text: At least one of P and Q is a magnet.
options.pick: Ask what attract can and cannot tell you. It needs a magnet, but the other object could be a magnet, iron or steel.
options.why: A magnet attracts iron, steel and the unlike pole of another magnet. All you can be sure of is that at least one is a magnet.

options.text: One is a magnet and the other must be an iron or steel block.
options.pick: Attract usually means a magnet pulling a magnetic material.
options.why: Two magnets attract too, when unlike poles face each other. The other object could also be a magnet.

options.text: Both are iron or steel blocks.
options.pick: Iron and steel are magnetic, so they seem to pull each other.
options.why: Two plain iron or steel blocks show no force on each other. A magnet is needed for any pull.

options.text: One is a magnet and the other is a wooden block.
options.pick: A magnet pulls things, so it might pull a wooden block.
options.why: A magnet shows no force with wood. Wood is non-magnetic.
